data.narrative:
Stacked Energy, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Dylan Erb and Sumitha Durairaj, operates within a frontier-tech sector populated by 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. The company has raised $98M to date.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation approach. The peer-median method was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Climate & Energy sector—while 8 total sector peers exist, none satisfy the narrow filters required to establish a statistically reliable peer set of three or more firms. The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $98M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $196M.

The triangulated range spans $167M (low) to $225M (high), centered at $196M (median). This single-method estimate carries material uncertainty: the absence of granular peer data limits validation of the 2.0x multiplier's applicability to Stacked Energy's specific risk profile and market position within frontier energy. A more robust range would require either identification of additional same-stage comparables or direct access to recent Series A terms in the sector. Key variables affecting valuation include technology readiness, path to commercialization, and capital efficiency relative to stated milestones.
